title: Stream of Characters
hints: you're always asking 'does some suffix ENDING at the newest character match a word' - reading a word backward from its last character is the same as reading its reverse forward from its first character
insert every dictionary word reversed into a trie (so 'cd' is stored as 'dc')
keep a running buffer of the stream seen so far (or just enough of its tail to cover the longest dictionary word)

on each new character, walk the reversed trie starting from the root, feeding it the stream's most recent characters in reverse order (newest first) - if you ever hit a node marked end-of-word during this walk, some suffix matches, return 1
if the walk falls off the trie (no child for the needed character) before hitting any end-of-word node, return 0 for this query
commonMistakes: storing dictionary words forward and trying to walk the trie backward, which doesn't correspond to any valid trie traversal
keeping the entire stream in memory and re-scanning all of it per query instead of only walking back up to the longest word length
not stopping the backward walk as soon as an end-of-word node is hit, which can waste time but more importantly risks missing that a SHORTER suffix already matched

content.problemStatement:
You're given a single space-delimited sequence of operations:

- the FIRST token always has the special form `init:word1,word2,word3` - a comma-separated dictionary of lowercase words (no spaces within a word), establishing the dictionary to check against
- every token after that has the form `query:c` where c is a single lowercase character, representing the next character arriving in a live stream (characters accumulate over time; you never see the whole stream at once)

**After each query character is appended to the stream so far, check whether the suffix of the stream ending at that character, for any length, exactly matches a complete word in the dictionary, and return a list with the result (1 if some suffix matches, else 0) for every query token, in order.**
constraints: dictionary words and stream characters consist only of lowercase English letters
notes: a query character that never contributes to any match, ever
a dictionary word of length 1 (matches immediately on the first occurrence of that character)
two different dictionary words that both end up matching at the same query position

sampleTestCases.input: ops = "init:cd,f,kl query:a query:b query:c query:d query:e query:f"
sampleTestCases.explanation: stream builds up as a,b,c,d,e,f; after the 4th character the stream is "abcd" and its suffix "cd" matches the dictionary; after the 6th character the stream is "abcdef" and its suffix "f" matches
every single character streamed is itself a suffix equal to the dictionary word "a"
stream becomes "xabc" only at the 4th character does the suffix "abc" match

optimal.pattern: insert the REVERSED dictionary words into a trie, then on each query walk backward from the most recently streamed character through the trie, stopping as soon as no reversed word can extend further or you hit an end-of-word node

bruteForce.approach: keep the whole stream seen so far as a string; on each query, try every suffix length and check if that suffix is in a set of dictionary words
bruteForce.time: O(max word length) per query if you cap suffix length checked, using a hash set for membership
